question: If $F(x)$ is an antiderivative of $f(x)$, show that $\dfrac{d}{dx} \int f(x)dx = f(x)$ using definition.
explanation:
By definition of indefinite integral:

$\int f(x)dx = F(x)+C$, where $F'(x)=f(x)$.

Differentiate both sides:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}(F(x)+C)=F'(x)$.

Since derivative of constant is zero, we get $F'(x)=f(x)$.

Hence $\dfrac{d}{dx}\int f(x)dx = f(x)$.
